name: Frugal Merchant Method
description: This Charm allows an Exalt to evaluate the quality of goods offered for sale, giving an intuitive sense of whether they are shoddy, exceptional, average or whatever. It does not give the character market knowledge he does not have — if he has no idea how much a good is supposed to cost, this power still will not tell him if he is being overcharged — and it grants no actual knowledge of the good under examination, only of its quality: presented with a totally unfamiliar object, the character can tell if it is shoddy or broken but will still know nothing of its purpose or operation. The Charm works on found objects as well as those offered for sale, and can, for example, tell whether a piece of First Age magic is still functional simply by handling it.

name: Insightful Buyer Technique
description: Through this Charm the character gains an intuitive feel for a marketplace at a given instant, allowing her to intuit roughly how much a given object will fetch in any one market. She need not be physically present, but the Charm must be used with a particular sales venue in mind; she cannot discover previously unknown markets with it, though she can review markets she is familiar with, even distant ones, to determine which would be the best place to sell a given good. The more specific the venue contemplated, the more accurate the forecast. The Charm is perfectly accurate if used at the moment of sale, but the more time elapses between its use and the actual sale, the greater the chance of an error in the projection.

name: Consumer-Evaluating Glance
description: An Exalt using this Charm may evaluate a given buyer's intentions and budget with but a glance. He can tell if a potential buyer has no real intention of purchasing, if she has already decided to buy, or if she requires swaying, and has a good idea of the target's budget for the purchase, at least in relation to the price he desires to obtain. He will also know if the target plans to attempt to swindle or betray him in some fashion, making this an essential tool for characters dealing in illegal or extremely valuable goods.

name: Irresistible Salesman Spirit
description: A character utilizing this Charm becomes the ultimate high-pressure salesman, able to sell practically anything to anyone for outrageous prices. If the target's Willpower is equal to or lower than the Exalt's Essence, he can be sold literally anything at any price — the Exalt may cause him to sell himself into slavery for a handful of potsherds or a kiss. If the target's Willpower is less than twice the Exalt's Essence, the player must make a Wits + Bureaucracy roll, and the number of successes is how many times the object's normal price the character manages to extract. The Charm does not work on characters whose Willpower is greater than twice the Exalt's Essence. It does not actually enforce the deal in any way and works only for a single scene; afterward the target will be acutely aware of having just been swindled, and the greater the swindle, the more likely he is to seek redress.

name: Deft Official's Way
description: An Exalt who uses this Charm becomes preternaturally adept at navigating bureaucracies, naturally sensing who to talk to in order to produce results, who expects or is amenable to bribes, which functionaries are actually useful or friendly and which are simply petty individuals enjoying their tiny sliver of power. A player whose character uses this Charm may add the character's Essence score in automatic successes to any Bureaucracy rolls when attempting to achieve a given result in a bureaucracy — obtaining a license, passport, grant or audience, for example. The Charm does not make the impossible possible, or allow an impoverished character to pay bribes she cannot afford, but it may allow her to find a way around such obstacles.

name: Speed the Wheels
description: Through this Charm a character can cause a bureaucracy to accomplish a task in record time, working (her Essence + 1) times faster for the duration of a particular job — so a character with Essence 3 expediting an appeal to a city's ruler for use of the naval dry-docks could make the appropriate appointments and cause the proper papers to be read four times faster than normal. This Charm simply speeds the process; it does not increase the character's chances of success. Characters who wish to improve their chances should use Social Charms or Deft Official's Way.

name: Indolent Official Charm
description: Solar Exalted can use their powers to slow as well as hasten the actions of a bureaucracy. Through this Charm a character may bring the wheels of government to a screeching, grinding halt with regard to a single task: papers will be lost at every turn, every petty official who could possibly interfere or request a bribe will do so, and petitions and requests will inevitably end up neglected at the bottom of the pile. For every point of Essence the character possesses, the amount of time the bureaucracy needs to accomplish the task is multiplied by one. The character need not be party to the matter to be delayed, but must know about the situation well enough to specify it; she may invest Essence speculatively — "the ongoing secret police investigation into my affair" is a perfectly valid target even if she is not sure one exists — but will not know whether the Charm had an effect, though as long as she keeps the Essence committed, an investigation meeting her criteria will be hampered. Each use can hinder the efforts of a number of investigators equal to (the character's Essence x 20).

name: Foul Air of Argument Technique
description: The character can cause a request, project or initiative to become the kiss of death for a bureaucracy. Meetings produce nothing, initiatives fall into pointless squabbling, and departmental infighting hampers even the simplest matters; worse, the fighting spreads, rippling out from the issue in question to other matters and eventually hampering or even crippling the bureaus involved. Bureaucracies subject to this Charm operate at a fraction of their efficiency equal to 1/(1 + the Essence score of the character) — a character with Essence 1 makes a bureau work at 1/2 efficiency, Essence 2 at 1/3, Essence 3 at 1/4, and so on. A character cannot use multiple invocations of this Charm on the same bureau at once.

name: Bureau-Rectifying Method
description: An Exalt who knows this Charm may use it to aid an investigation of corruption in a bureaucracy; she must either request or take part in the investigation. The result will be an actual investigation — genuine inquiries, real punishments and potentially even meaningful reform. Used by an Exalt heading an investigation, it causes questioned individuals to be much more cooperative than they would otherwise be, and subordinates who would otherwise go through the motions of their jobs will instead actually attempt to ferret out the corruption. There is a finite upper limit on how wide-ranging an investigation this Charm can support: typically an Exalt can bolster the efforts of (her Essence rating x 20) individuals per use, and if she is reforming an entire bureaucracy the Storyteller should feel free to force her to commit Essence more than once. The Charm does not cause an investigation to be launched, merely reinforces one already in progress.

name: Bureaucratic Concealment Technique
description: Using this Charm, a character can effectively cause a single item to disappear into the depths of a bureaucracy and remain hidden from all efforts to find it until the Exalted ceases committing Essence to the Charm or chooses to retrieve the item herself. The item may be virtually anything that can be moved through human effort: a letter, an artifact, a piece of jewelry — even a statue or the like. It is shuffled from place to place, stored and forgotten, and it draws no attention to itself. Investigation attempts to find the concealed item have their difficulty increased by the Exalted's Essence.

name: Forgetful Bureau Charm
description:
Forgetful Bureau Charm allows an Exalted character to erase all evidence of one item or individual from a particular bureaucracy. Records are lost or destroyed, officials misremember facts, and so forth. The effects take some time to make themselves felt. A small local bureaucracy is affected within a day. Larger organizations may take weeks, or even months, before the process is complete. So far as the bureaucracy is concerned, the item or individual in question does not exist. Those with direct contact with the subject still recall it normally, but official records and other documentation do not support their recollections. New records can come into being after this Charm is used, but previous records on the subject are permanently lost.

This Charm allows the Chosen to create difficulties for others by eliminating all official record of them or for the Exalted to protect their own secrets, such as removing evidence of a Circle's activities or of the location of a particular Demesne or Manse.
